title: WPMS/3488/2019 of SHANKAR LAL CHAUDHARY Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
WPMS No. 3488 of 2019
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. B.S. Negi, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. V.D. Bisen, Brief Holder for the
State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. V.S. Rawat, Advocate for respondent
nos. 5 & 6.
Heard learned counsel for the parties
through video conferencing.
This writ petition has been filed by Mr.
Shankar Lal Chaudhary, who claims to be the
Manager/Priest of Holy Harju Temple,
Gangolihat.
Petitioner is aggrieved by the notice
issued by Nagar Panchayat, Gangolihat,
whereby petitioner has been asked to remove
his encroachment from public land, failing
which, the same shall be removed under
provisions of Municipalities Act, 1916.
A counter affidavit has been filed by Mr.
Ashish Negi, Executive Officer, Nagar
Panchayat, Gangolihat. In paragraph no. 7 of
the counter affidavit, it has been stated that
the contention of the petitioner that the
temple was constructed on the land of one
Mr. Jeevan Lal Chaudhary is incorrect, as in
the revenue records, Khet No. 1200 and 1201
are recorded in the name of Mandir Chawk
Chaubhadi, under Class 10 (2) Category.
Learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that the temple has been
constructed over a private land of one Mr.
Jeevan Lal Chaudhary, which was donated by
him to the temple, therefore, according to
him, the stand taken in the counter affidavit
is incorrect.
Having regard to the facts &
circumstances of the case, the writ petition is
disposed of with liberty to petitioner to make
representation to S.D.M., Gangolihat, within
ten days from today, for joint inspection of
the land in question by municipal and

revenue officials. If such representation is
made within the stipulated period, the S.D.M.
concerned shall constitute a team of revenue
and municipal officials, which shall inspect
the site in presence of the petitioner and
submit the report within three weeks, as to
whether the temple is constructed over public
land or not. The S.D.M. concerned shall,
thereafter, pass appropriate order, in
accordance with law, within two weeks from
the date of receipt of report of the inspection.
Learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that if any gate/boundary wall of the
temple incidentally encroaches upon the
public land, then petitioner will voluntarily
remove the gate/boundary wall of the temple.
For a period of two months or till
passing of final order by the S.D.M.,
whichever is earlier, status quo, as of today,
shall be maintained by the parties.
